correctness.rationale: PASS: Maximality is equivalent to unmatched independence. The independent-set bound excludes matchings with at most four edges. Two distinct exhaustive enumerators independently exclude all five-edge maximal matchings, enumerate exactly 192 six-edge minima, and reconstruct the same exchange graph. Exhaustive all-source BFS establishes connectivity, radius and diameter, while full 384-element group action verifies orbit counts and edge types; both programs were run and their outputs recorded.

evidence: Minimum maximal matching and edge domination number have equal optimum scalar value, but arbitrary minimum edge dominating sets need not be matchings. Baste et al., arXiv:1905.12241, introduction, defines the minimum maximal matching parameter.

The claimed graph uses only size-six maximal matchings and set differences of size one or two; perfect matching, induced matching and edge dominating sets without the matching constraint are not equivalent configuration spaces.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: We tested alternate names minimum maximal matching, edge-domination number, minimum edge-dominating matching, saturation matching, independent edge domination, hypercube/binary cube and edge exchange. The scalar edge domination equivalence does not entail any all-optima exchange graph, especially because its set of minimizers need not equal the set of maximal matchings.

value.rationale: PASS: The target is the natural entire set of optimal edge-dominating matchings in a classical small regular graph, not an arbitrary selection. The one-to-two simultaneous exchange threshold quantifies how many resources must be rerouted at once to retain optimality, and the exact orbit and metric data identify nontrivial asymmetry and transport cost. These facts do not follow from the optimum cardinality or known approximation bounds.
